diffuseAlbedo.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.subsurfaceReference.diffuseReflectance (Jensen, Marschner, Levoy & Hanrahan 2001, a white marble, measured)
diffuseAlbedo.note: A white crystalline marble measured whole: the nearest specimen to a white statuary Carrara. The camera's channels are read as the Rec.709 primaries.

refractiveIndex.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.specularF0 (0.0533, calcite grains in random orientations)
refractiveIndex.derivation: n = (1 + sqrt(F0)) / (1 - sqrt(F0)), the index whose normal-incidence reflectance is the record's F0

porosity.source: Mandarin Stone, 'Product Specification: Calacatta Marble': EN 1936 apparent density 2680 kg/m3 and open porosity 0.30 %; EN 13755 water absorption 0.10 %. https://www.mandarinstone.com/app/uploads/2017/09/Calacatta-Marble-Mandarin-Stone-Data-Sheet-1.pdf
porosity.note: The values match the sheet. It is a transfer: the sheet is for Calacatta, not Statuario, and it states no quarry or origin. The Apuan origin comes from the trade name only. The value is plausible for a dense Carrara-type calcite marble and agrees with the record's old 'a few tenths of a per cent'.

wettingDepth.source: Palette.json: accent.statuario realMaterial (white statuary marble, faint grey veins)
wettingDepth.note: As the Crema Marfil: a dense stone wets only its outer millimetre.

grain.source: Harbord, Brantut & Wallis (2023), 'Grain-size effects during semi-brittle flow of calcite rocks', arXiv:2302.01183, abstract: Carrara marble average grain size 200 µm. Read at https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.01183
grain.note: Confirmed. The source gives 200 µm for laboratory Carrara marble, not for a Statuario block, so the grade stays secondary.

bed.source: Palette.json: accent.statuario realMaterial (white statuary marble, faint grey veins)
bed.note: The faint grey veins a statuary block shows, a first spacing read from trade photographs.

bedAspect.source: Palette.json: accent.statuario realMaterial (white statuary marble, faint grey veins)
bedAspect.note: The veins are drawn out along the block's schistosity, finer across it.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, J. Geophys. Res. Solid Earth 117, B08409, doi:10.1029/2011JB009041, abstract (read via https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1029/2011JB009041).
hurst.note: The exponents are confirmed from the abstract; section 4.1 is unverified. This is a transfer from natural fault surfaces to a carved and honed marble face.

toneSpread.source: Palette.json: accent.statuario realMaterial (white statuary marble, faint grey veins)
toneSpread.note: Statuary is the most even of the Carrara grades: a faint tonal spread.

roughnessSpread.source: Workings/honed.json: unverified surface.microRoughness (no filtered roughness read)
roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across a worked face, as the travertine's.

absorption.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.subsurfaceReference.absorption (Jensen, Marschner, Levoy & Hanrahan 2001, a white marble, measured)
absorption.note: The measured white marble itself: light diffuses millimetres into the calcite before it leaves.

scattering.source: Substances/cream-marble.json: optics.subsurfaceReference.reducedScattering (Jensen, Marschner, Levoy & Hanrahan 2001, a white marble, measured)
